answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a refundable stake: each new identity locks a deposit, like an opal held in escrow, and earns trust only through verified work over time. Spawning thousands of fakes then costs real money, while an honest agent gets its ivory-white deposit back in full. If an agent cheats, the stake is slashed, so a gale of cheap clones cannot outrun the price of every burned bond.
